messages:
ivy: Heads-up: I ran the reconnect fuzz harness against sampleapp v0.12 + node-sdk@1.4.3 and hit a few parsing anomalies. Repro rate ~1% with random kill/restart intervals 30-250ms.

ivy: Symptoms: sometimes two `data:` lines from consecutive connections are merged into one event payload, other times an `id:` from new conn shows up before a blank-line delimiter from prev conn so parser emits empty event then the merged payload.

ivy: Minimal tcpdump snippet (abbrev):
```
--- conn A tail ---
data: {"seq":42,"msg":"partA"}

--- conn B head ---
id: 43
data: {"seq":43,"msg":"partB"}

# observed parsed output (bad):
{"seq":42,"msg":"partA"}
{id: 43}
data: {"seq":43,"msg":"partB"}
# and node parser collapsed into single data value: "{...}\n{id: 43}\ndata: {...}" which breaks JSON parsing
```

marco: thanks for the harness. can you share the fuzz script? curious about timing distribution.

ivy: it's under dev-tools/fuzz/reconnect-fuzz.sh in my branch. basically spawn client -> sleep random(30..250ms) -> kill -9 -> spawn. I also tried SIGINT vs SIGTERM vs SIGKILL; Kill type affects kernel shutdown semantics. SIGKILL produced more RSTs and higher merge rate.

zhen: interesting that SIGKILL spikes incidence. kernel RST will drop pending bytes, but if client closed without flushing CRLF, parser buffer will still be non-empty on server side until new bytes appended. Two-layer fix set: client SDK should clear parser state on socket `close`/`error`; server should always append explicit blank line and flush after event.

marco: quick triage on node parser: it waits for a blank line to emit assembled event. If socket ends with partial event (no blank line) it currently leaves buffer intact. We could either drop partial on close, or emit it as a comment `:partial` to avoid JSON parse attempts. Both need opt-in flag to avoid surprising users.

ivy: I prototyped the comment approach with opt-in flag `ssePartialComment=true`. Behavior: on `close` emit `:partial-truncated\n` then the partial payload as a comment line, then reset buffer. That prevented JSON crashes in sample apps.

zhen: I favor comment approach as backwards-compatible (won't break strict parsers). Also add a parser heuristic: treat a leading `id:`/`event:` without preceding blank line as implicit delimiter (only when `ssePartialComment` is enabled). That catches reconns where server sends `id:` at start.

marco: can you drop a small patch? I'll review and we can backport to 1.3.x if clean. Also add an integration test simulating SIGKILL followed by immediate reconnect so CI won't regress.

ivy: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/857 — adds `parser.on('close', ...)` comment emission, the `ssePartialComment` flag, and test harness using `child_process` to simulate abrupt exits.

ops-bot: Created issue DEVEX-2258: "SSE: reconnect-fuzz reveals partial buffer merges on rapid reconnects" (link: https://tracker.internal/DEVEX-2258)

zhen: long-term: consider metadata `id` seq numbers from server so clients can detect merged frames and either reject or re-request missing parts. But that's heavier. For now, client fix + sampleapp flush + fuzz tests should be enough.

marco: agreed. I'll schedule backport to 1.3 and coordinate with releng. Ivy, please add a short note in streaming.md about immediate reconnect edge-case and how to enable `ssePartialComment` during demos.

ivy: done. I also uploaded a short video capture to the PR showing before/after parsing. Thanks team.
